library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gong_2025_talquetamab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gong_2025_talquetamab"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70004>

Talquetamab is a GPRC5D x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager approved for
relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) at two subcutaneous recommended
phase II doses (RP2Ds): 0.4 mg/kg weekly (QW) and 0.8 mg/kg every other week
(Q2W), each preceded by step-up doses. Gong 2025 reports the clinical
pharmacology of the phase I/II MonumenTAL-1 study, including a population PK
model whose structure and estimates are given in Supporting Information
Figure S5 and Table S5.

The model has two compartments, a sequential zero-order (duration `D1`) then
first-order (`Ka`) subcutaneous absorption, and a clearance that declines over
time from its value at treatment start, `CL0`:

$$ CL(t) = CL_0 \cdot CL_{PCT} + CL_0 \cdot (1 - CL_{PCT}) \cdot e^{-K_{DES}\,t}, \qquad t \text{ in days.} $$

`CLPCT` is the fraction of `CL0` that remains at steady state. Gong 2025
attributes the decline to falling tumour burden or target level, disease
severity or cancer cachexia, as reported for nivolumab, teclistamab and
daratumumab.

# Population

The population PK dataset held 5354 measurable serum talquetamab concentrations
from 492 patients, 100 dosed intravenously and 392 subcutaneously. Patients had
a median age of 65 years (range 33-86) and a median weight of 74.8 kg (range
40.2-143); 42.7% were female and 86.2% White. Baseline ISS stage was I in
44.1%, II in 33.5% and III in 20.9%; 50.2% had IgG myeloma (Gong 2025 Table S4,
overall column).

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gong_2025_talquetamab"))$population
str(pop, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

Every value comes from Gong 2025 **Table S5** ("Parameter estimates for final
population PK model") and its footnotes; the structure is **Figure S5**.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL0) | 2.08 L/day | Table S5, RSE 6.58% |
| `cl_exp_famp` (CLPCT - 1) | 0.512 - 1 | Table S5 CLPCT = 0.512, RSE 4.32% |
| `lcl_exp_kdes` (KDES) | 0.0229 1/day | Table S5, RSE 7.21% |
| `lvc` (V1) | 4.30 L | Table S5, RSE 2.54% |
| `lq` (Q) | 1.01 L/day | Table S5, RSE 6.10% |
| `lvp` (V2) | 5.78 L | Table S5, RSE 8.59% |
| `lka` (Ka) | 0.138 1/day | Table S5, RSE 5.47% |
| `lfdepot` (F) | 0.619 | Table S5, RSE 4.58% |
| `ld1` (D1) | 0.142 day | Table S5, RSE 19.6% |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.672 | Table S5 "BWT on CL0", footnote a |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.670 | Table S5 "BWT on V1", footnote b |
| `e_mm_nigg_cl` | -0.547 | Table S5 "IgG or non-IgG on CL0"; footnote a factor 0.453 |
| `e_iss_ii_iii_cl` | 0.318 | Table S5 "ISS II or III on CL0"; footnote a factor 1.318 |
| `etalcl`, `etacl_exp_famp`, `etalvc`, `etalcl_exp_kdes`, `etalq`, `etalvp`, `etalka`, `etalfdepot`, `etald1` | log(1 + CV^2) with CV 51.7, 59.7, 22.3, 67.4, 39.4, 82.8, 65.9, 80.8, 145.3% | Table S5 IIV column |
| `propSd` | 0.220 | Table S5 "Proportional error (CV%)" |
| `CL0 = 2.08 (BWT/74.8)^0.672 0.453^{non-IgG} 1.318^{ISS II/III}` | n/a | Table S5 footnote a |
| `CL = CL0 CLPCT + CL0 (1 - CLPCT) exp(-0.0229 t)` | n/a | Table S5 footnote a; Figure S5 |
| `V1 = 4.30 (BWT/74.8)^0.670` | n/a | Table S5 footnote b |
| 2 compartments, SC input zero-order over D1 into depot then Ka; IV into central | n/a | Results; Figure S5 |

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. Three arms of 150 virtual patients each are given
the schedules simulated in Gong 2025 Figure 3:

* **QW RP2D**: step-up doses 0.01 and 0.06 mg/kg, then 0.4 mg/kg weekly.
* **Q2W RP2D (studied)**: step-up doses 0.01, 0.06 and 0.3 mg/kg, then 0.8 mg/kg every 2 weeks.
* **Q2W RP2D (approved)**: step-up doses 0.01, 0.06 and 0.4 mg/kg, then 0.8 mg/kg every 2 weeks.

Gong 2025 Figure 4 places the Q2W step-up doses on days -6, -4 and -2 before
the first full dose on day 0. The QW step-up days are not printed; days -4 and
-2 match where the QW curve starts in Figure 3a. The model clock starts at the
first step-up dose, because `KDES` acts on time since the first dose.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() fixes the covariate draws below; rxode2's own random-effect draws
# are not reproducible across builds, so the checks downstream target medians
# and typical values rather than cohort extremes.
set.seed(20250701)
n_per_arm <- 150L

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                  ~stepup,              ~full, ~tau,
  "0.4 mg/kg QW",        c(0.01, 0.06),        0.4,   7,
  "0.8 mg/kg Q2W",       c(0.01, 0.06, 0.3),   0.8,   14,
  "0.8 mg/kg Q2W (0.4 step-up)", c(0.01, 0.06, 0.4), 0.8, 14
)

n_weeks_full <- 10    # long enough for the Q2W cycle 3 day 1 interval (days 56-70)

make_doses <- function(stepup, full, tau) {
  t_full0 <- 2 * length(stepup)                 # step-ups 2 days apart
  full_times <- seq(t_full0, t_full0 + 7 * n_weeks_full - tau, by = tau)
  tibble(
    time = c(seq(0, by = 2, length.out = length(stepup)), full_times),
    mgkg = c(stepup, rep(full, length(full_times))),
    t_c1d1 = t_full0
  )
}

# Covariates: Table S4 overall column. WT median 74.8 kg (range 40.2-143);
# ISS I/II/III 217/165/103 of the 485 with a stage; non-IgG 245 of 492.
subj <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(3L * n_per_arm),
  arm = rep(arms$arm, each = n_per_arm),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(3L * n_per_arm, log(74.8), 0.22), 40.2), 143),
  iss = sample(c("I", "II", "III"), 3L * n_per_arm, replace = TRUE,
               prob = c(217, 165, 103) / 485),
  MM_NIGG = rbinom(3L * n_per_arm, 1L, 245 / 492)
) |>
  mutate(ISS_II = as.integer(iss == "II"), ISS_III = as.integer(iss == "III"))

dose_rows <- subj |>
  inner_join(
    arms |> rowwise() |> reframe(arm, make_doses(stepup, full, tau)),
    by = "arm", relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  mutate(amt = mgkg * WT, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2)

t_c1d1 <- dose_rows |> distinct(arm, t_c1d1)

obs_times <- seq(0, 6 + 7 * n_weeks_full, by = 0.25)
obs_rows <- subj |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = NA_real_)

events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, WT, ISS_II, ISS_III, MM_NIGG)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Gong_2025_talquetamab")

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("WT", "MM_NIGG", "ISS_II", "ISS_III")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  left_join(subj |> select(id, arm), by = "id") |>
  left_join(t_c1d1, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(time_c1d1 = time - t_c1d1)

stopifnot(nrow(sim) > 0, all(sim$Cc >= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## Concentration-time profiles (replicates Figure 3)

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 7}
prof <- sim |>
  filter(time_c1d1 <= 56) |>
  group_by(arm, time_c1d1) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

prof_a <- prof |> filter(arm != "0.8 mg/kg Q2W (0.4 step-up)") |> mutate(panel = "(a) RP2Ds")
prof_b <- prof |> filter(arm != "0.4 mg/kg QW") |> mutate(panel = "(b) Q2W step-up schedules")

bind_rows(prof_a, prof_b) |>
  filter(Q50 > 0.5) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_c1d1 / 7, Q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 0.5), ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 353, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.5, 1e4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since cycle 1 day 1 dose (weeks)",
    y = "Talquetamab concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Gong 2025: median and 90% interval. Dashed line: maximum EC90, 353 ng/mL."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Both RP2D medians sit well above the maximum EC90 of 353 ng/mL after the first
full dose, and the 5th percentile hovers around it, as Gong 2025 states.
The two Q2W step-up schedules give overlapping profiles (Figure 3b).

```{r ec90}
ec90_tab <- sim |>
  filter(arm != "0.8 mg/kg Q2W (0.4 step-up)",
         time_c1d1 %in% c(7 * (1:8))) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    `Median of predose concentrations, weeks 1-8 (ng/mL)` = median(Cc),
    `Predose samples above 353 ng/mL (%)` = 100 * mean(Cc >= 353),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(ec90_tab, digits = 0)
```

# PKNCA validation

Gong 2025 Table S3 reports phase I NCA at the RP2Ds after the cycle 1 day 1 and
cycle 3 day 1 full doses: day 0 and day 42 for QW (21-day cycles) and day 0 and
day 56 for Q2W (28-day cycles). Each dosing interval is passed to PKNCA as its
own group with time re-zeroed at the dose.

```{r pknca}
windows <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,             ~interval,       ~start, ~tau,
  "0.4 mg/kg QW",   "Cycle 1 day 1", 0,      7,
  "0.4 mg/kg QW",   "Cycle 3 day 1", 42,     7,
  "0.8 mg/kg Q2W",  "Cycle 1 day 1", 0,      14,
  "0.8 mg/kg Q2W",  "Cycle 3 day 1", 56,     14
)

sim_nca <- windows |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(
    sim |>
      filter(arm == .env$arm, time_c1d1 >= start, time_c1d1 <= start + tau) |>
      mutate(interval = .env$interval, time_rel = time_c1d1 - .env$start)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(arm, interval, sep = ", ")) |>
  select(id, treatment, arm, interval, time_rel, Cc)

dose_nca <- sim_nca |>
  distinct(id, treatment, arm) |>
  left_join(subj |> select(id, WT), by = "id") |>
  mutate(time_rel = 0, amt = ifelse(arm == "0.4 mg/kg QW", 0.4, 0.8) * WT)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(as.data.frame(sim_nca), Cc ~ time_rel | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(as.data.frame(dose_nca), amt ~ time_rel | treatment + id)

intervals_all <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(treatment = c("0.4 mg/kg QW, Cycle 1 day 1", "0.4 mg/kg QW, Cycle 3 day 1"),
             start = 0, end = 7),
  data.frame(treatment = c("0.8 mg/kg Q2W, Cycle 1 day 1", "0.8 mg/kg Q2W, Cycle 3 day 1"),
             start = 0, end = 14)
) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_all))

# Table S3 trough = 'observed predose analyte concentration at the start of
# the dosing interval', i.e. the concentration at time_rel = 0.
predose <- sim_nca |> filter(time_rel == 0) |> select(treatment, id, ctrough = Cc)

nca_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(predose, by = c("treatment", "id")) |>
  mutate(auclast = auclast * 24)        # ng*day/mL -> ng*h/mL as in Table S3

stopifnot(nrow(nca_ind) == 4L * n_per_arm)
```

## Side-by-side comparison with Table S3

Table S3 gives arithmetic means (and the median for tmax), so the simulated
values are summarised the same way before the comparison.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                     ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~cav,  ~ctrough,
  "0.4 mg/kg QW, Cycle 1 day 1",  1568,  2.93,  178101,   1060,  178,
  "0.4 mg/kg QW, Cycle 3 day 1",  3799,  2.01,  607297,   3615,  2548,
  "0.8 mg/kg Q2W, Cycle 1 day 1", 2507,  2.83,  675764,   2011,  597,
  "0.8 mg/kg Q2W, Cycle 3 day 1", 4161,  2.85,  1021059,  3039,  1831
)

sim_summary <- nca_ind |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = mean(cmax), tmax = median(tmax), auclast = mean(auclast),
    cav = mean(cav), ctrough = mean(ctrough), .groups = "drop"
  )

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_summary,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "day", auclast = "ng*h/mL", cav = "ng/mL", ctrough = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs Gong 2025 Table S3 (means; tmax median). * differs by > 20%.")
```

The phase I NCA in Table S3 came from 13-33 patients per cell, with
coefficients of variation of 40-90%, so differences of 20-40% from a
population-model simulation of the whole phase I/II population are within the
sampling noise of the observed means. The observed tmax comes from the sparse
phase I schedule (samples on days 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 or 9 after the dose; Table
S1), so it is quantised differently from the 6-hour simulated grid and is
expected to sit a day or so earlier. The 0.4 mg/kg QW cycle 1 values run
lower than observed; they are also the most sensitive to the QW step-up
timing, which Gong 2025 does not print (see Assumptions).

## Terminal half-life (Results)

Gong 2025 reports a median terminal half-life of **7.56 days at initial
treatment** and **12.2 days at steady state**. The individual terminal
(beta-phase) half-life is computed from each subject's micro-constants with
`CL = CL0` at the start and `CL = CL0 * CLPCT` at steady state.

```{r half-life}
beta_half_life <- function(cl, vc, q, vp) {
  k10 <- cl / vc; k12 <- q / vc; k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  log(2) / beta
}

hl <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    clpct_i = 1 + cl_exp_famp_i,
    thalf_start = beta_half_life(cl0, vc, q, vp),
    thalf_ss = beta_half_life(cl0 * clpct_i, vc, q, vp)
  )

hl_tab <- tibble(
  Quantity = c("Median terminal half-life at initial treatment (day)",
               "Median terminal half-life at steady state (day)"),
  Simulated = c(median(hl$thalf_start), median(hl$thalf_ss)),
  Published = c(7.56, 12.2)
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Simulated - Published) / Published)
knitr::kable(hl_tab, digits = 2)
```

# Covariate effects on exposure (Figure 4)

Figure 4 of Gong 2025 reports the geometric-mean ratio of `Cavg,4weeks` (the
average concentration over the first 4 weeks of full doses) at the 0.8 mg/kg
Q2W RP2D: **2.0** for non-IgG vs IgG myeloma, **0.77** for ISS stage II and
**0.71** for stage III vs stage I. Those are ratios of post hoc exposures and
carry the cohort's covariate correlations; the typical-value ratios below
isolate each model effect.

```{r covariates}
typ_events <- function(nigg, iss23) {
  d <- make_doses(c(0.01, 0.06, 0.3), 0.8, 14)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = 1L, time = d$time, amt = d$mgkg * 74.8, rate = -2, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 6 + 28, by = 0.05), amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
           evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(WT = 74.8, MM_NIGG = nigg, ISS_II = iss23, ISS_III = 0L)
}

cavg4 <- function(nigg, iss23) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events(nigg, iss23)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    filter(time >= 6, time <= 34)
  sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 28
}

ref <- cavg4(0L, 0L)
cov_tab <- tibble(
  Comparison = c("Non-IgG vs IgG myeloma", "ISS II or III vs ISS I"),
  `Typical-value ratio` = c(cavg4(1L, 0L) / ref, cavg4(0L, 1L) / ref),
  `Figure 4 GMR` = c("2.0 (1.8-2.1)", "0.77 (II); 0.71 (III)")
)
knitr::kable(cov_tab, digits = 2)
```

The non-IgG factor of 0.453 on `CL0` gives a typical-value ratio at the lower
end of the published interval, and the single pooled ISS factor of 1.318
lands between the stage II and stage III ratios, as expected when one
coefficient serves both stages.

The typical-value `Cavg,4weeks` at the Q2W RP2D for a 74.8 kg IgG, ISS I
patient is `r round(ref)` ng/mL. Gong 2025 Figure 5a shows the RP2D exposures
spanning roughly 100 to 5000 ng/mL with medians near 1000-1500 ng/mL.

```{r cavg-cohort}
sim |>
  filter(arm != "0.8 mg/kg Q2W (0.4 step-up)", time_c1d1 >= 0, time_c1d1 <= 28) |>
  group_by(arm, id) |>
  summarise(cavg4 = sum(diff(time_c1d1) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) / 28,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(median = median(cavg4), Q25 = quantile(cavg4, 0.25),
            Q75 = quantile(cavg4, 0.75), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Simulated Cavg,4weeks (ng/mL); compare the Figure 5a box plots.")
```

# Steady state (Results)

Gong 2025 reports that steady state (90% of the steady-state concentration) was
reached at week 16 for both RP2Ds. Because the clearance falls with `KDES`
(half-time `r round(log(2) / 0.0229)` days), steady state depends on both
accumulation and the clearance decline. The typical-value interval average for
an IgG, ISS I patient is compared with its value after one year.

```{r steady-state}
ss_profile <- function(stepup, full, tau) {
  d <- make_doses(stepup, full, tau)
  t0 <- d$t_c1d1[1]
  full_times <- seq(t0, t0 + 400, by = tau)
  ev <- bind_rows(
    tibble(time = c(seq(0, by = 2, length.out = length(stepup)), full_times),
           amt = c(stepup, rep(full, length(full_times))) * 74.8,
           rate = -2, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(time = seq(0, t0 + 400, by = 0.25), amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
           evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(id = 1L, WT = 74.8, MM_NIGG = 0L, ISS_II = 0L, ISS_III = 0L)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev) |> as.data.frame()
  tibble(start = head(full_times, -1)) |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(cavg = {
      w <- s[s$time >= start & s$time <= start + tau, ]
      sum(diff(w$time) * (head(w$Cc, -1) + tail(w$Cc, -1)) / 2) / tau
    }) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(week = (start - t0) / 7)
}

ss <- bind_rows(
  ss_profile(c(0.01, 0.06), 0.4, 7) |> mutate(arm = "0.4 mg/kg QW"),
  ss_profile(c(0.01, 0.06, 0.3), 0.8, 14) |> mutate(arm = "0.8 mg/kg Q2W")
) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  mutate(frac_ss = cavg / cavg[week == max(week[week <= 52])]) |>
  ungroup()

ss_week <- ss |>
  filter(frac_ss >= 0.9) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(`First week with Cavg >= 90% of the 1-year value` = min(week), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(ss_week)

ggplot(ss |> filter(week <= 40), aes(week, frac_ss, colour = arm)) +
  geom_step() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 16, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "Week of full-dose treatment", y = "Interval Cavg / 1-year value",
       colour = NULL, caption = "Dotted line: week 16, where Gong 2025 reports steady state.")
```

The typical patient reaches 90% of the steady-state interval average a little
before week 16; Gong 2025's figure is a population summary across patients
whose `KDES` varies with a 67% CV, so a later population-level time is
expected.

# Validation gate

```{r gate}
stopifnot(
  # Half-lives: a mis-transcribed CL0, CLPCT, Q or V2 moves these by tens of percent.
  abs(hl_tab$`Difference (%)`[1]) < 20,
  abs(hl_tab$`Difference (%)`[2]) < 20,
  # Covariate effects (typical value, deterministic).
  abs(cov_tab$`Typical-value ratio`[1] / 2.0 - 1) < 0.15,
  cov_tab$`Typical-value ratio`[2] > 0.68, cov_tab$`Typical-value ratio`[2] < 0.80,
  # Exposure centre: simulated mean Cavg in every Table S3 cell within a factor
  # of 1.6 of the published mean.
  all(abs(log(sim_summary$cav / published$cav[match(sim_summary$treatment, published$treatment)])) < log(1.6))
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV distribution of the fractional parameters.** Gong 2025 Methods state
  that every random effect was log-normal, and Table S5 reports IIV as CV% on
  CLPCT (59.7%) and F (80.8%) as on the other parameters. They are encoded
  log-normally as stated, so some simulated patients have F > 1 or CLPCT > 1
  (a clearance that rises rather than falls over time). A logit transform,
  common for fractions, is not described and was not substituted.
* **CV to variance.** The paper does not state its CV definition; the exact
  log-normal relation `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` is used for every eta. No
  covariances are reported, so the etas are independent.
* **CLPCT parameterisation.** The model stores CLPCT as the registered signed
  amplitude `cl_exp_famp = CLPCT - 1`, so `cl = CL0 * (1 + cl_exp_famp * (1 -
  exp(-KDES t)))`; this is algebraically identical to Table S5 footnote a. The
  CLPCT eta multiplies CLPCT itself.
* **Pooled ISS effect.** Gong 2025 estimates one factor (1.318) for ISS stage II
  or III; the model applies it as `(1 + 0.318 * (ISS_II + ISS_III))`. Figure 4's
  separate 0.77 and 0.71 ratios come from post hoc exposures, not from separate
  model terms.
* **Residual error.** Table S5 lists "Proportional error (CV%)" as 0.220; it is
  read as a 22% proportional error (`propSd = 0.220`).
* **Step-up timing.** The QW step-up days (-4 and -2 before the first full dose)
  are read from where the QW curve starts in Figure 3a; the Q2W days (-6, -4,
  -2) are printed in the Figure 4 caption.
* **Dose level.** Phase I used 0.405 mg/kg QW and phase II 0.4 mg/kg; 0.4 mg/kg
  is simulated throughout, a 1.2% difference.
* **Exposure-response models.** The ORR logistic/Emax regressions, the
  Kaplan-Meier analyses and the safety quartile analyses are not encoded: their
  coefficients are not reported (Table S6 gives only odds ratios for MM subtype
  and extramedullary plasmacytoma, with a flat exposure term).
